articles.text:
INVL Secures €70.6 Million To Start Investing In Central And Eastern European Banks
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 1:00 PM
INVL Secures €70.6 Million To Start Investing In Central And Eastern European Banks
INVL Asset Management has secured €70.6 million in commitments at the first close of its European Banking Opportunities Fund, giving it capital to begin investing in banks across Central and Eastern Europe. The fund attracted 41 investors from Lithuania, Latvia and Estonia, and Invalda INVL is committing €10 million. The first close came earlier than planned. INVL is targeting up to €200 million and plans further closes in 2027.
A Mandate For Controlling And Minority Stakes
The closed-end fund will focus on lenders in Central and Eastern European countries that are European Union members or pursuing EU membership. INVL says it will seek out banks where it can help support growth. The fund can acquire controlling or minority stakes and participate in capital increases, allowing it to invest in existing shares or provide fresh equity to a bank.
The Bank of Lithuania approved the fund’s rules in October 2026. Individual investments may also require approval from the relevant banking supervisors, depending on the size of the stake and the laws that apply to the transaction.
Building On Existing Regional Banking Investments
Invalda INVL has operated in the financial sector for more than three decades and already holds stakes in two regional lenders. Together with an INVL fund, it owns more than 14% of maib, Moldova’s largest bank. It is also the largest shareholder in Lithuania’s Artea, with a stake of almost 20%.
INVL Family Office distributed the fund’s units. Its head, Asta Jovaišienė, said demand from Baltic investors helped bring the first close forward. She expects the next close in 2027 to draw new investors and sees room for some existing investors to increase their commitments.
KEY QUOTE
“Baltic investors showed keen interest in the opportunity to take part in private equity transactions in the banking sector, which meant the first close was completed earlier than planned. We believe that the second close in 2027 will attract new investors, and that some existing investors will increase their commitments.”
Asta Jovaišienė, Head Of INVL Family Office

articles.title: Latham & Watkins Partner Josh Hamilton Joins Westside Ronald McDonald House Board
articles.snippet:
Josh Hamilton, a Latham & Watkins partner and trial lawyer, has been elected to the board of trustees of Ronald McDonald House Westside Los Angeles. The nonprofit is raising $50 million to turn a former boutique hotel in Westwood Village into a four-story, 33,000-square-foot house for families of hospitalized children.
The post Latham & Watkins Partner Josh Hamilton Joins Westside Ronald McDonald House Board appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Latham & Watkins Partner Josh Hamilton Joins Westside Ronald McDonald House Board
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 11:10 AM
Latham & Watkins Partner Josh Hamilton Joins Westside Ronald McDonald House Board
Josh Hamilton, a Latham & Watkins partner and trial lawyer, has been elected to the board of trustees of Ronald McDonald House Westside Los Angeles. The nonprofit is raising $50 million to turn a former boutique hotel in Westwood Village into a four-story, 33,000-square-foot house for families of hospitalized children.
The planned facility will provide lodging, meals, laundry facilities and communal spaces at no cost. It will serve families whose children receive treatment at UCLA Children’s Hospital and Cedars-Sinai Guerin Children’s. The Westside house is the seventh in the Southern California chapter.
Hamilton previously co-chaired Latham’s Los Angeles litigation and trial department. His practice covers complex commercial, securities and corporate governance disputes, and he advises companies and their boards on governance and disclosure. He also serves on the board of trustees of Crossroads School for Arts & Sciences and previously served on the boards of the Western Center on Law and Poverty and the Independent School Alliance for Minority Affairs.
KEY QUOTE
“Josh’s background, expertise and enthusiastic support of our mission makes him a wonderful addition to our board of trustees. His love for the Los Angeles community and his dedication to support children and their families perfectly aligns with our objective of removing barriers so families of hospitalized children can focus on what matters most: their child.”
Kelly Herman, Executive Director Of Ronald McDonald House Westside Los Angeles

articles.title: Bcomp Secures €20 Million In EIB Venture Debt For Romanian Flax Composite Plant
articles.snippet:
The European Investment Bank is providing €20 million in venture debt to Swiss materials company Bcomp to help build a high-volume manufacturing plant in Timișoara, Romania, and expand research and development in Fribourg, Switzerland.
The post Bcomp Secures €20 Million In EIB Venture Debt For Romanian Flax Composite Plant appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Bcomp Secures €20 Million In EIB Venture Debt For Romanian Flax Composite Plant
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 11:09 AM
Bcomp Secures €20 Million In EIB Venture Debt For Romanian Flax Composite Plant
The European Investment Bank is providing €20 million in venture debt to Swiss materials company Bcomp to help build a high-volume manufacturing plant in Timișoara, Romania, and expand research and development in Fribourg, Switzerland.
The financing, backed by the European Union’s InvestEU program, supports a €47.6 million investment program planned for 2027 through 2030. Approximately 61% of the investment will take place in Romania’s Vest region, where Bcomp expects the new plant to drive workforce growth.
Bcomp makes lightweight reinforcement materials primarily from flax fibers. Its products are designed as alternatives to conventional carbon fiber, glass fiber and plastics in applications including automotive parts, motorsport and recreational equipment. The Romanian facility will increase manufacturing capacity while Bcomp continues to develop its materials and manufacturing processes in Switzerland.
KEY QUOTES
“Europe needs to turn technological innovation into industrial production if we are to strengthen our competitiveness and accelerate the green transition. By supporting Bcomp in Romania and Switzerland, we are helping European innovation reach industrial scale and unlock new opportunities for sustainable growth.”
Ioannis Tsakiris, Vice President Of The European Investment Bank
“Scaling up our natural fibre composites production is an important step towards making these materials available to more manufacturers and applications, while supporting the EU’s transition towards a circular economy. The EIB’s support will allow us to expand production and continue investing in R&D, strengthening our ability to serve industrial customers and accelerating the adoption of our high-performance natural fibre materials.”
Christian Fischer, Chief Executive Officer Of Bcomp
